I could not derive this exponent from first principles or confirm it against the literature, so this answer is a best recollection rather than a verified result.

The heuristic I considered: hyperbolic volume grows like $e^{(d-1)\rho}$ at distance $\rho$, so the second moment of the restricted zero cell is governed by how fast the probability of the cell reaching distance $\rho$ decays at criticality. A polynomial divergence $R^\alpha$ in every dimension suggests a dimension-free polynomial correction to that decay. Matching the known result to a dimension-independent power, my recollection points to $\alpha = 3$, but I did not check this against the source.

ANSWER: 3
